raw:
EPA METHANE RULE — CREATOR STORYBOARD
Target length: 4:30

SCENE 1 — FEAR (8s)
HEADLINE: 72 HOURS OF FLARING
NARRATION: Seventy-two hours. That is how long some oil and gas operators can now burn off gas during certain malfunctions, instead of twenty-four.
VISUAL: A gas flare burning at night over a dark field. Slow push in.
AUDIO: Low drone, then silence before the last word.
SOURCES: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/14/2026-20001/oil-and-natural-gas-sector

SCENE 2 — FEAR (10s)
HEADLINE: "DOES NOT CONCERN HUMAN HEALTH"
NARRATION: In the rule explaining that change, the EPA wrote that "this action does not concern human health."
VISUAL: The rule's text, enlarged around the sentence.
AUDIO: A single low tone.

SCENE 3 — FEAR (12s)
HEADLINE: WHO LIVES NEAR THE FLARES?
NARRATION: Families living near well pads breathe what a flare does not burn. Children breathe more air per pound of body weight than adults.
VISUAL: A school playground with a well pad on the horizon.
AUDIO: Distant children's voices, faded.

SCENE 4 — FEAR (9s)
HEADLINE: WHAT IS IN THE SMOKE
NARRATION: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas, and flares can release other pollutants when they do not burn completely.
VISUAL: Close-up of a flare stack against the sky.

SCENE 5 — ANGER (11s)
HEADLINE: THE CHILDREN'S HEALTH POLICY
NARRATION: The EPA has a policy on children's health. Because the agency decided this action does not concern human health, it said that policy does not apply.
VISUAL: EPA policy document, highlighted.

SCENE 6 — ANGER (10s)
HEADLINE: WHAT WAS ASSESSED?
NARRATION: So what did the agency assess before deciding? The rule's own analysis is where the answer should be.
VISUAL: Slow pan across the docket index.

SCENE 7 — ANGER (12s)
HEADLINE: $45 BILLION
NARRATION: The EPA estimates the proposal would save the industry about $45 billion. It is proposed, not final.
VISUAL: A data card with the figure and the word PROPOSED.

SCENE 8 — ANGER (10s)
HEADLINE: EPA'S EXPLANATION
NARRATION: The agency says the change means fewer wells shut in, and longer flaring only where the alternative would emit more.
VISUAL: The EPA's explanation, quoted on screen.

SCENE 9 — ANGER (9s)
HEADLINE: A NARROW READING
NARRATION: That is a legal reading of when a rule "concerns" health. Critics say it is too narrow.
VISUAL: Two quotes side by side.

SCENE 10 — ANGER (11s)
HEADLINE: WHO IS WATCHING?
NARRATION: The Super Emitter Program lets approved third parties report large methane releases from space and from the air.
VISUAL: Aircraft over a field of wells.

SCENE 11 — ANGER (10s)
HEADLINE: THE PROPOSAL
NARRATION: In October, the EPA proposed changes to how that program works.
VISUAL: The October proposal's first page.

SCENE 12 — MOTIVATION (12s)
HEADLINE: NOVEMBER 16–17: PUBLIC HEARING
NARRATION: You can speak. The EPA holds a virtual public hearing on November 16 and 17.
VISUAL: A laptop showing the hearing registration page.
AUDIO: Music lifts.

SCENE 13 — MOTIVATION (10s)
HEADLINE: DECEMBER 16: WRITTEN COMMENTS
NARRATION: Written comments are due December 16.
VISUAL: The regulations.gov docket page.

SCENE 14 — MOTIVATION (8s)
HEADLINE: JODYTRACKS.COM
NARRATION: Follow the rule, and every record behind this story, at jodytracks.com.
VISUAL: JODY logo end card.
AUDIO: Music resolves.
